record.file_problem: None; the full post, including appendices and comments, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The post experimentally tests hand-coded conditional circuits embedded in a network, not feature storage or any of the six claim versions. Its discussion distinguishes computation in superposition from storing features in superposition; it neither tests nor relies on the claim’s feature-geometry finding.
record.gate_note: The post cites Toy Models of Superposition as an example of feature storage, but explicitly distinguishes that from implementing computations in superposition. Its reported outcomes concern conditional-rotation circuits, their errors, and error predictions; they do not measure feature directions, polysemanticity, LLM representations, SAE features, or feature dimensionality. The post’s theoretical parameter ratios and plotted predictions are not experimental outcomes by themselves.
record.test_reason: The post hand-codes conditional-rotation circuits into a ReLU MLP and measures computation errors. It does not train networks or measure learned feature geometry, polysemanticity, LLM representations, SAE features, or feature dimensionality. The superposition embedding is imposed by construction, not observed arising. It cites Toy Models of Superposition only to contrast storage with computation in superposition.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is essentially correct. The authors conclude the method works but errors compound and explode beyond a modest number of circuits. They state that implementing independent computations in superposition is much harder and costlier than storing features in superposition. They also speculate that real LLMs may have far fewer independent circuits than often assumed.
record.recipe_differences: This is a hand-coded embedding of conditional rotation circuits into a ReLU MLP, with a modified circuit-embedding construction; it is not a test of the original Toy Models of Superposition feature-storage experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported errors increase with the number of simultaneously active circuits z, depth, and network loading (including Td²/D²); outcomes also differ between active and inactive circuits and between average and worst-case error.

fits_no_version.finding: In a hand-coded ReLU MLP, about 2D/d conditional-rotation circuits (557 circuits at D=1000) work for only 2–4 layers before errors compound superlinearly.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Computation in superposition across layers is far costlier than storage. Interference noise compounds with depth, active-circuit count and the Td²/D² ratio, limiting the number of independent circuits.

fits_no_version.finding: Error theory fits when errors are small, and undershoots once noise switches on inactive ReLUs; the authors call this a cascading 'seizure'.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Errors in hand-coded computation-in-superposition constructions cascade once noise crosses ReLU thresholds.

record.problems: The evaluation is on hand-coded toy circuits, not trained models or feature representations. The post notes that its error calculations are approximate and apply only while errors stay small; some terms are guessed and checked empirically. Worst-case results for z>1 fluctuate somewhat with sample size. Many plotted values are not transcribed numerically in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. The post also reports inactive rotating-vector error comparisons (Figure 9) and active-neuron fractions (Figure 7), but gives no separate textual outcome specific enough to add beyond the reported error-growth and cascading-failure results.

untested.parts: Learned sparse-feature storage, near-orthogonal directions, sparsity-dependent transition, regular geometry.
Capacity competition as the cause of polysemanticity.
Distributed or sparse features in LLMs. The comments mention GPT-2 parameter decomposition anecdotally, with no results.
Completeness, stability or canonicity of SAE features.
Dimensionality of superposed features; the rotated vectors are 2-D by design, which is not a test.

record.verdict_notes: This is an engineering/theory-check post on a hand-coded network. Superposition is imposed by construction, so no version can receive a verdict. All rows evaluate the authors' own construction against their own predictions. The record's 'partial' states are not meaningful against any version and are reset to cannot_determine.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test sparse feature storage, near-orthogonal feature directions, a sparsity-dependent transition, or regular feature geometry.
Does not test polysemantic neurons or capacity competition between features.
Does not test causes of polysemanticity outside capacity pressure.

Does not test whether dictionary features are complete, stable, or canonical.
Does not test whether represented features are one-dimensional directions.

tranche.reason: The construction uses overlapping superposition embeddings to implement conditional rotations and reports its own computational errors. It uses superposition as a tool without testing any listed claim version.
